title: New winter rates saved at least $37M for Massachusetts heat-pump…
summary: Canary Media 2026: Massachusetts seasonal heat pump rates saved owners money; RI and NY consider similar discounts on delivery charges.

assertions.quote: Massachusetts consumers with home heat pumps saved some $37 million on their power bills — an average of more than $250 per customer
Worries about high electricity rates, however, have been a more stubborn barrier to adoption, particularly for homeowners heating with natural gas
72% of current natural gas customers would save money by switching to a heat pump if discounted rates were adopted, up from 27%
That number jumps to 64% with the existing heat pump discount and could go up to almost 82% if the deeper proposed cuts are implemented.
The logic behind these discounts is that traditional electricity rates overcharge heat pump owners for their share of grid construction and upkeep.

verdicts.note: In summer-peaking systems winter load adds little grid cost, so volumetric delivery charges overcharge heat pumps, but this fades as grids turn winter-peaking.
